Just another tip to help you increase your running; try interval training. The best way to enjoy and improve your running is to mix it up and confuse the body. Running the same route at the same pace every time will become boring and counter productive.

Interval training: while out running at your normal pace, look ahead to a marking of your choice and sprint at about 80% of your max (you'll soon learn what that means to you) and then slow down to a walk for about twice the distance of your sprint. Pick up speed again and sprint to the next marker etc. Keep repeating until you're knackered but not dead and are still able to get home ;)

The general rule of thumb is to increase 10% a week for 3 weeks with your 4th week being a recover. So if you do 2.5 miles now for 3 days a week, you'd bump that up to 2.75 miles a day, then 3 miles, then 3.25 miles, then go back to 2 or 2.5 miles for a week. The next cycle you'd start at 3.25 miles, go to 3.5, then 3.8, then back to 3. It doesn't sound like much but that's the idea. You want to increase your distances slowly. Go to far, to fast, and you'll risk injury. For me, I usually bump things up a mile or two at a time but everyone's different. If you get shin splints, slow down. You could apply the same rule to your time instead of your distance but that's more of a personal choice I think.

On your off days, I'd recommend yoga if you can stand it. Same for core and upper-body work. Swimming and biking are great alternatives too. And don't forget to take a rest day. Even from walking. Your body needs it.

So you're currently running 6 to 8 MPW over 3 days.

Do this: Tu 3 miles Thu 3 miles Sat 5 miles Repeat for 3 weeks

Then adjust:

Tu 4m Wed 2m easy Thu 3m Sat 5m Repeat for 3 weeks

After that, gradually increase your mileage by no more than 1.5 to 2 miles per week up to about 15 and continue to do that until you've lost whatever weight you're trying to lose.

Stick to the Tu-Wed-Thu-Sat plan. Wednesday is always an easy run (e.g., very slow; if you run 10 minute miles on other days, run 11:30 on Wednesdays). Add a short (2 mile, easy) recovery run on Sunday if you want. Gradually make your Tuesday runs your fast days where you feel like covering the distance at the speed you're going is tough (i.e., tempo). Keep your Saturday runs at an easy comfortable place. This might feel embarrassingly or awkwardly slow at first. Run Thursday on feel. If you feel good, run faster. If you feel bombed out and depleted, run slower. Walk if you have to, just cover the miles.
